newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan dlr ends sharply up on recent intervention.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan dlr ends sharply up on recent intervention.

text.p: In a sharp reverse, the Taiwan dollar closed higher against its U.S. counterpart on Thursday as the central bank's recent defence finally boosted buying sentiment, dealers said.
The local unit ended at T$27.855 against Wednesday's T$27.926 finish.
Turnover through dealers was heavy at US$380 million.
Wednesday's T$27.926 finish was the Taiwan dollar's lowest level since it closed at T$28.03 on January 7, 1989.
Dealers said the central bank intervened quietly but firmly on Wednesday to avert an even sharper loss, and the moves apparently succeeded in triggering a rebound on Thursday.
"The central bank made it clear it wanted to stop the fall, and investors finally got the point today (Thursday)," said one dealer at a foreign bank.
"The rise clearly indicates that investors believe the U.S. dollar has hit a short-term peak," he said.

Taiwan's currency has been on a slow decline since early 1997, with senior analysts polled by Reuters forecasting that the rate would slip to T$28 to the U.S. dollar in the second half -- but only when the central bank is ready.
Dealers said they expected a wide trading range for Friday, with investors again seeking to test the central bank's "bottom line" for the local currency.
